title: Gartley and Bat
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/0/body: The **Gartley** is a five-point pattern (X, A, B, C, D) named after **H.M. Gartley**, who introduced it in his 1935 book. The bullish version looks like the letter **M**, and at D we look to **buy**.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/1/body: What makes a Gartley a Gartley is its ratios: **B at 61.8%** of XA and **D at 78.6%** of XA. So D always stays **inside** the XA leg; in a bullish pattern, that means above X.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/1/tip: The Gartley is also called the "222 pattern", because it appears on page 222 of Gartley's book.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/2/prompt: Is this Gartley on the yen bullish or bearish, and what trade do we look for at D?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/2/explanat: X is the pattern's high, and D ended below X but above B; the overall shape looks like a W. This is a bearish Gartley, so at D we look for a sell signal.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/3/prompt: We have a bullish Gartley on EUR/USD. Where's point D (the 78.6% retracement of XA)?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/4/prompt: Bullish Gartley on gold: X = 2300 and A = 2400. Mark point D (the 78.6% retracement of XA) with the line.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/4/explanat: The XA leg is $100 (2300 to 2400). In a Gartley, D sits at the 78.6% retracement of XA: 2400 − 0.786 × 100 = 2321.4. That's the middle of the PRZ; traders still wait for a reversal signal to enter, and put the stop loss just below X.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/5/statemen: In a bullish Gartley, point D forms below X.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/5/explanat: D is at 78.6% of XA, so it's still inside the XA leg and above X. If price goes below X, it's no longer a Gartley.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/6/body: A Gartley's last three legs usually form an **ABCD**. When **78.6% of XA** lands close to **AB=CD** and the BC projection, the Gartley's **PRZ** is formed. If price closes **below X**, the pattern is invalid.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/7/prompt: This is a bullish Gartley. Tap the candle that formed point D at 78.6% of XA.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/7/explanat: This candle's lower wick reached the 78.6% XA line exactly and closed higher. That's where D completed, and price bounced up after it.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/8/sentence: In a Gartley, B forms at ___ and D at ___ of the XA leg.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/8/explanat: These two numbers are the Gartley's signature: B at 61.8% and D at 78.6% of XA.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/9/prompt: A bullish Gartley has completed in the PRZ, and the last candle is a hammer. What do you do?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l1/steps/9/explanat: D sits at 78.6% of XA and AB=CD, and the hammer shows buyers stepping in. A move back up is more likely. Stop loss below X (58,000), because below X the Gartley is no longer valid.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/0/body: The **Bat** was introduced by **Scott Carney**. It looks like a Gartley, but the points sit at different depths: **B is shallower** (38.2 to 50 percent of XA) and **D is deeper** (88.6% of XA), very close to X.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/1/body: In a Bat, the CD leg is usually **longer than AB** and has a bigger BC projection. Its most important number is **0.886 XA** for point D.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/2/prompt: We have a bullish Bat on GBP/USD. Where's point D (the 88.6% retracement of XA)?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/3/prompt: B formed at 50% and D at 88.6% of the XA leg. Which pattern is this?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/3/explanat: A shallow B (50%) and a deep D (88.6%) are the Bat's signature. In a Gartley, B sits around 61.8% and D at 78.6%.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/4/statemen: In a Bat, point B is usually shallower than a Gartley's B.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/4/explanat: A Bat's B retraces 38.2 to 50 percent of XA, while a Gartley's B retraces around 61.8%.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/5/title: The Bat's edge: a tight stop loss
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/5/body: Because a Bat's D sits at **88.6%**, close to X, a **stop loss beyond X** is only a short distance from your entry. That means less risk per trade and the chance of a **better risk-to-reward**.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/6/prompt: Where's a sensible stop loss for a bullish Bat?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/6/explanat: If price goes past X, D is no longer at 88.6% and the pattern is invalid, so a stop loss beyond X makes sense. B, C and the 78.6% level are all above your entry.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/7/prompt: This is a bearish Bat. Tap the candle that formed D at 88.6% of XA.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/7/explanat: This candle's upper wick reached 88.6% of XA (2438.6) exactly and closed lower. That's D, and price dropped after it.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/8/prompt: A bearish Bat has completed at 88.6% of XA, and the last candle is a shooting star. What's your call?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l2/steps/8/explanat: D sits at 88.6% of XA, and the shooting star shows buyers couldn't hold price up. A move back down is more likely. A stop loss above X (1.0950) is only about 23 pips from D.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/0/title: The key difference: the depth of B and D
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/0/body: The Gartley and the Bat both have **D inside XA**, but at different depths: in a Gartley, B is around **61.8%** and D at **78.6%**; in a Bat, B is shallower (**38.2 to 50%**) and D deeper (**88.6%**).
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/1/body: Point **B** forms before D and tells you which pattern to look for: B at 61.8% means expect D at **78.6%**; B between 38.2 and 50 percent means **88.6%**.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/1/tip: If B lands somewhere between the two, the pattern isn't standard, and many traders skip it.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/3/prompt: This pattern's B sits at 61.8% of XA, and price is heading toward D. At which level do you expect D?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/3/explanat: B at 61.8% means a Gartley is probably forming, so watch for D at 78.6% of XA (around 148.43).
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/4/prompt: We have these three points on EUR/USD. Which pattern is probably forming, and where's D?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/4/explanat: B retraced only 90 of 200 pips, or 45%: Bat depth. A Bat's D is at 88.6%: 1.1000 − 0.0177 = 1.0823.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/5/body: If you put the stop loss for both patterns **beyond X**, the Bat usually has **less risk**, because its D is closer to X. In a Gartley, D is further from X, so the stop loss is wider.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/5/example/: Risk with a 5-pip buffer beyond X
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/5/tip: Less risk doesn't mean a better pattern; the Bat also needs price confirmation in the PRZ.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/6/statemen: In the Gartley and the Bat, point D forms inside the XA leg and doesn't go past X.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/6/explanat: Both are retracement patterns: D is at 78.6% or 88.6% of XA. Patterns whose D goes past X (the Butterfly and the Crab) are coming up in the next unit.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/7/prompt: Put the steps for spotting a Gartley or a Bat in order.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/7/items/3: Check AB=CD and the BC projection
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/7/items/4: Wait for price confirmation in the PRZ
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/7/explanat: First the base leg (XA), then B's depth, which reveals the pattern type, then the D level and other confirmations, and last of all, price's reaction in the PRZ.
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/8/prompt: B was at 50% of XA, and now D has completed at 88.6% of XA with a shooting star. What's your call?
lessons/harmonics-u2-l3/steps/8/explanat: B at 50% and D at 88.6% means a bearish Bat. A reversal candle in the PRZ raises the odds of a drop (not certain); stop loss just above X (66,000).
